headline: Funding flows. Satellites soar. Tensions rise.
deck: This week features a mix of funding boosts, strategic satellite maneuvers, and rising geopolitical tensions in space.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, emphasizing its focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The funding highlights the Department of Defense's increasing reliance on commercial capabilities for national security. With a valuation now pegged at $1.6 billion, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the defense space.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that space security will be a hot commodity, but it remains to be seen if True Anomaly can deliver beyond the cash.

stories.head: Vast enters national security with new division
stories.body: Vast has launched a dedicated division for national security projects, aiming to secure contracts in a space increasingly defined by defense needs. This move comes as the company seeks to capitalize on growing government interest in private sector solutions. With the U.S. military ramping up its space operations, Vast is betting on its ability to navigate this complex landscape.
stories.soWhat: Vast's pivot to defense could be a sign that even space startups are realizing they need to play the government game to survive.

stories.head: FCC clears C-band for 5G, complicating satellite ops
stories.body: The FCC has approved sweeping reforms that will push satellite operators out of more C-band spectrum to facilitate a 5G auction. This decision could significantly impact companies relying on this spectrum for satellite communications, with potential revenue implications. As the 5G landscape evolves, satellite operators may find themselves squeezed between terrestrial demands and orbital ambitions.
stories.soWhat: This move could be a wake-up call for satellite operators that the terrestrial world is not going to wait for them to catch up.

watchlist.title: Watch for more funding rounds next week
watchlist.body: With True Anomaly's success, expect other startups to ramp up their fundraising efforts, particularly in defense and security.

watchlist.title: Potential fallout from FCC's C-band decision
watchlist.body: Satellite companies will need to reassess their strategies in light of the FCC's new regulations, which could lead to consolidation.

watchlist.title: Vast's contracts could reshape defense landscape
watchlist.body: If Vast secures significant contracts, it could signal a new trend of startups becoming essential players in national security.

watchlist.title: Implications of Shijian-31's orbit
watchlist.body: China's unique orbit for Shijian-31 may prompt U.S. operators to rethink their own orbital strategies and capabilities.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
